title: Getting started with comdynamite
text: draw tree 40 species, give optima strong phylogenetic signal (Brownian motion, lambda = 1), let close relatives compete strongly. sim$abundance holds abundance species site last step. Ordering sites environment species optimum shows sorting species along gradient:
code: tr <- ape::rcoal(40) traits <- species_traits(tr, lambda = 1) alpha <- competition_matrix(tr, type = "phylo", inter_max = 0.1) land <- landscape_implicit(n_sites = 50)  sim <- simulate_metacommunity(land, traits, alpha, dispersal = 0.01, n_steps = 500) sim #> <mc_sim> 50 sites x 40 species #> species persisting: 29 of 40  #> mean local richness: 10.9 a <- sim$abundance[order(land$env), order(traits$optimum)] image(log1p(a), xlab = "sites (by environment)", ylab = "species (by optimum)",       axes = FALSE, col = hcl.colors(20, "YlGnBu", rev = TRUE))

title: Getting started with comdynamite
text: Dispersal changes regime. low dispersal, species occur environment suits (species sorting); high dispersal, also occur unsuitable sites kept supplied immigrants (mass effects), local richness increases composition tracks environment less closely.
code: regimes <- c(sorting = 0.01, mass_effects = 0.5) res <- lapply(regimes, function(d)   simulate_metacommunity(land, traits, alpha, dispersal = d, n_steps = 500)) sapply(res, function(s) c(   mean_richness = mean(rowSums(s$abundance > 0)),   persisting = sum(colSums(s$abundance) > 0) )) #>               sorting mass_effects #> mean_richness   10.74        19.74 #> persisting      30.00        21.00

title: Getting started with comdynamite
text: landscape_grid() places sites grid, default wrapped torus, spatially autocorrelated environment exponential dispersal kernel.  spatial structure, sites longer exchangeable, permuting sites random valid null model. torus_permutations() gives rearrangements torus (translations eight symmetries square) keep distances among sites, therefore spatial autocorrelation environment:
code: grid <- landscape_grid(side = 10, env_bandwidth = 2, disp_scale = 2) image(matrix(grid$env, 10, 10), asp = 1, axes = FALSE,       col = hcl.colors(20, "Earth"), main = "environment") sim_sp <- simulate_metacommunity(grid, traits, alpha, dispersal = 0.1, n_steps = 500) sim_sp #> <mc_sim> 100 sites x 40 species #> species persisting: 29 of 40  #> mean local richness: 19.4 perms <- torus_permutations(10) dim(perms) #> [1] 799 100 # the environment under the first rearrangement env_perm <- grid$env[perms[1, ]]

what: An environment that changes over time
title: Getting started with comdynamite
text: env_over_time() adds autocorrelated temporal fluctuations environment site, record_steps keeps abundances chosen steps.
code: et <- env_over_time(land$env, n_steps = 500, rho = 0.95, sd = 5) sim_t <- simulate_metacommunity(land, traits, alpha, dispersal = 0.01, n_steps = 500,                                 env_time = et, record_steps = seq(100, 500, 100)) apply(sim_t$history > 0, 3, function(x) mean(rowSums(x))) #> step100 step200 step300 step400 step500  #>   12.96   10.18    9.84    9.22    9.54

what: Traits under one or several adaptive optima
title: Getting started with comdynamite
text: traits_ou() simulates traits Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process (Hansen 1997). alpha = 0 Brownian motion; alpha > 0 traits pulled towards optimum, paint_regimes() gives clades optimum (multi-peak OU; Butler & King 2004).
code: pool <- ape::rcoal(32) node <- ape::getMRCA(pool, pool$tip.label[1:8]) in_clade <- rownames(traits_ou(pool)) %in% ape::extract.clade(pool, node)$tip.label reg <- paint_regimes(pool, nodes = node) x_ou <- traits_ou(pool, alpha = 2, theta = c(`0` = 0, `1` = 5), regimes = reg) tapply(x_ou[, 1], ifelse(in_clade, "clade (optimum 5)", "rest (optimum 0)"), mean) #> clade (optimum 5)  rest (optimum 0)  #>         4.7336002         0.2932017

title: Getting started with comdynamite
text: Besides population dynamics, comdynamite can assemble local community regional pool fixed rules, Kraft et al. (2007). Species removed one time community reaches chosen size: "limiting_similarity": GAUSE algorithm Colwell & Winkler (1984), Kraft et al. (2007) used competition. pair species closest trait space, one smaller sum distances remaining species removed, . "filtering": species farthest niche optimum (ancestral state derived corner trait space) removed first. "neutral": species drawn random. many pools, mean phylogenetic distance (MPD) among community members shows expected contrast traits evolve Brownian motion: average, limiting similarity keeps distant relatives neutral assembly (higher MPD), filtering keeps closer relatives (lower MPD), although single replicates vary.
code: pool <- ape::rcoal(32) x <- traits_ou(pool, n_traits = 2) assemble_community(x, size = 16, rule = "limiting_similarity")$community #>  [1] "t18" "t25" "t31" "t29" "t8"  "t1"  "t4"  "t12" "t17" "t19" "t27" "t5"  #> [13] "t15" "t13" "t3"  "t9" mpd <- function(tree, sp) mean(as.dist(ape::cophenetic.phylo(tree)[sp, sp])) rules <- c("limiting_similarity", "filtering", "neutral") res <- replicate(100, {   pool <- ape::rcoal(32)   x <- traits_ou(pool, n_traits = 2)   sapply(rules, function(r) mpd(pool, assemble_community(x, 16, r)$community)) }) rowMeans(res) #> limiting_similarity           filtering             neutral  #>            2.152022            1.620627            2.052095

what: Traits evolving by an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with one or several optima — traits_ou
title: Traits evolving by an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with one or several optima — traits_ou
text: Simulates traits along tree Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) model Hansen (1997), multi-optimum ("multi-peak") extension Butler & King (2004). Along branch trait pulled towards optimum theta selective regime branch strength alpha, drifting rate sigma2. Values drawn exactly transition distribution process: branch length t, trait value x start , end, normal distribution mean theta + (x - theta) * exp(-alpha * t) variance sigma2 / (2 * alpha) * (1 - exp(-2 * alpha * t)).

title: Traits evolving by an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with one or several optima — traits_ou
text: tree rooted phylo tree branch lengths. n_traits Number independent traits. alpha Strength selection towards optimum (0 = Brownian motion). sigma2 Rate stochastic (drift) component. theta Optimum regime: one value single optimum, named vector one value per regime (names regimes). regimes Selective regime branch, order edges tree reordered "cladewise" (ape::reorder.phylo(tree, "cladewise")), returned paint_regimes(). NULL puts every branch one regime. root Trait value root.

text: First version: model Thompson et al. (2020) phylogenetic traits competition, spatially implicit grid landscapes, torus permutations time-varying environments. Code pcps-sim project. Rule-based assembly (assemble_community()): limiting similarity (GAUSE algorithm Colwell & Winkler 1984), habitat filtering neutral assembly, Kraft et al. (2007). traits_ou(): traits Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process one several optima (multi-peak OU; Brownian motion alpha = 0), paint_regimes() assign regimes clades.
